open: [STUB] Ring Two's food stalls, Hearthline, and somewhere down the row a loader is arguing with a scanner. A stallholder slaps a receipt on her counter: forty bowls, paid, never collected. An off-shift crew holds up its own receipt for the same order and swears it was collected and paid for twice. If nobody settles it before the market bell, the crew boycotts her stall and the Exchange clerk logs a complaint. The bell hangs overhead.

clean.text: [STUB] She counts it out loud: half of forty bowls is twenty, and twenty she can carry. Their boss shrugs and takes the split while onions fry somewhere above. Both receipts go onto one spike. Word travels down Ring Two that this quarrel ended without a clerk, and two brokers nod at your crew.

cost.text: [STUB] Her half will not come out of the till, so the difference lands on your crew's tab: a thousand credits, counted into a dented tin. In return their foreman tears his receipt in two in front of the stall. Twenty bowls go out still warm. She keeps the tin close and does not say thank you.

fail.text: [STUB] Half is still too much, she says, and the crew boss calls her a thief over the counter. Nobody moves toward the middle. Market lines are noisy again, and the shouting carries three stalls in both directions. Her last word is that she will take her receipt to the registry office herself after the bell. Glaring, their foreman watches your crew go down the row.

clean.text: [STUB] Under the counter, the stall's own tally shows the order of forty bowls paid twice, once in coin and once on the crew's tab. One order, two payments. Pale over her books, the stallholder strikes the second line through and initials it. Lidded bowls come out for the crew, on the house. Tempers along the row cool by a degree.

cost.text: [STUB] Metre by metre the till's paper roll comes out across the counter, with the stallholder hovering over every inch. Nothing is wrong with her scale. A jammed till printed the order twice, and both receipts carry the same serial. Lips tight, she refunds the crew and slides five hundred credits across for the trouble. From then on she prices your crew's bowls like a stranger's.

fail.text: [STUB] Slamming shut, her books catch a crewmate's fingers before the second page turns. No one touches her scale without a registry stamp, she says. That ends it. Five hundred credits go into her jar to cover the inspection already done. Duplicate slips for every Ring Two order sit at the broker's booth by the water reclaimer until tomorrow's opening.

clean.text: [STUB] Summoned from the Exchange, the clerk reads both receipts side by side and finds the crew's stamped a minute later. Paid twice, then. A refund of one payment is ordered on the spot, and a thousand credits land on your crew's account as a witness fee. Every word of it sours her face. Forty bowls leave the counter before the bell.

cost.text: [STUB] By the clerk's ruling the order stands paid once, the crew's second payment comes back, and whoever called the Exchange covers the filing. Five hundred credits leave your crew's account for the stamp. Up on the post goes the ruling. Behind the counter the stallholder wipes one spot over and over, and she will not serve your crew again this week.

fail.text: [STUB] At the word clerk the stallholder snatches both receipts and pins them under her cash box. Nobody is calling anyone, she says. Shouting starts from the crew boss, and a second crew drifts over to watch. With the bell this close, the clerk's desk will hear the dispute only on the morning shift, filed in person at the Exchange window. Until then the noise follows your crew.

ending: [STUB] The market bell rings over Ring Two's food stalls, and your crew stands at the edge of Hearthline's noise. The ledger card follows.
